data.what_it_does: Generates glue code between Flutter/Dart and Rust, allowing you to seamlessly call Rust code from Dart and vice versa. It supports arbitrary types, async Rust, traits, and complex data structures without manual boilerplate.
use_when: You need high-performance Rust code for CPU-heavy computations or data-intensive operations in Flutter.
You want to reuse existing Rust libraries or codebases within a cross-platform mobile, desktop, or web Flutter app.
avoid_when: Your application does not require performance-critical native code or systems programming capabilities.
You want to avoid external toolchains such as Cargo and Rust compilation steps in your project workflow.
strengths: Supports arbitrary Rust and Dart types, asynchronous Rust, and two-way communication (Rust calling Dart).
Officially recognized as a Flutter Favorite package with strong reliability and CI coverage.
weaknesses: Requires setting up and managing a Rust toolchain alongside your Flutter development environment.
Build times and project complexity can increase due to cross-compilation requirements for multiple platforms.
data.setup_notes: Requires installing cargo install flutter_rust_bridge_codegen, setting up a Rust directory in your project, and running code generation commands.

alternatives.name: ffi
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer writing manual Dart FFI bindings without an external code generator.
